questions.q: What event type fires when a new object is uploaded to S3?
options: s3:BucketCreated
s3:ObjectDeleted
lambda:Invoke
s3:ObjectCreated:Put
questions.explain: s3:ObjectCreated:Put (and related ObjectCreated variants) is the event type an S3 notification matches to invoke a target like Lambda.

questions.q: What information does S3 pass to the Lambda function when it invokes it via a trigger?
options: The full contents of the object, embedded in the event
The bucket name and the object key
Only the object's file size
Nothing — the function must poll S3 to find out what changed
questions.explain: The event payload contains the bucket and key; the function typically fetches the object itself using that information.

questions.q: What do prefix and suffix filters on an S3 event notification let you do?
options: Limit how many times a Lambda function can be invoked per day
Encrypt objects before they reach Lambda
Restrict which objects trigger the notification, e.g. only .csv files under a raw/ prefix
Automatically convert file formats before invocation
questions.explain: Filters let a bucket with several file types route only matching objects to the Lambda function meant to handle them.

questions.q: What does a resource-based policy on a Lambda function do in the S3-trigger pattern?
options: Grants the function permission to read from S3
Grants the S3 service principal permission to invoke the function
Encrypts the function's environment variables
Grants IAM users permission to edit the function's code
questions.explain: The resource-based policy is what allows S3 (s3.amazonaws.com) to call into Lambda; without it, S3 can't invoke the function at all.

questions.q: A Lambda function is invoked successfully on every S3 upload but fails with access-denied when it tries to read the object. What's most likely missing?
options: The resource-based policy is missing
The function has exceeded its memory limit
The execution role lacks S3 read permissions
The event notification filter is misconfigured
questions.explain: Successful invocation means the resource-based policy is fine; an access-denied error when reading S3 points to a missing permission on the function's own execution role.
